newsitem.title: FRANCE: BAe seeks integrated Airbus company.
newsitem.headline: BAe seeks integrated Airbus company.

text.p: A senior executive of British Aerospace Plc said on Thursday that he would like to see the European Airbus consortium change into an integrated company with its own factories and form part of a larger civil and military grouping.
Airbus Industrie is in the midst of changing to a joint stock company from a four-strong partnership and there are different views on what shape the new entity will take.

"We would like to see a future Airbus company which has control of the facilities, the assets and the skills that they need to be a full player in the civil aircraft market and a real competitor to Boeing," John Weston, group managing director of British Aerospace (BAe) told a business conference.
BAe is an Airbus partner, along with French state-owned SNI Aerospatiale, Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas (Casa) of Spain.

"We would like to see that business have sufficient strength, a sufficiently strong balance sheet, to meet the challenges of financing the sales of the number of aircraft that we believe the expansion in the market is going to drive," Weston said.
Aerospatiale's chairman Yves Michot has said he sees the new Airbus as essentially a major prime contractor, directing the work of suppliers and retaining its design offices.

Weston said all the partners and the governments agreed on adopting a company status, the need to streamline decision making and to improve competitiveness. But because the structure of each partner company is different and the Airbus work is mingled in their factories with other programmes, there are difficulties in implementing the change in each country, he said.

"I don't think we are talking here about significant differences in where we would like to get to, but we are talking about very significant differences in the starting points and we've got a lot of work to do to find our way to a practical and pragmatic solution," he said.

Weston saw the future of Airbus as the civil aircraft division of large European entity, which would also have a combat aircraft and missiles division. That grouping would absorb BAe and other national firms to compete with U.S. giants across civilian and military markets.
That European entity would have shareholders in all the countries and would have industrial and technical facilities, which would make it attractive to each of the governments.
If Airbus were part of that grouping, it could draw on valuable military technology developed on defence budgets, similar to U.S. companies that have both arms, he said.
